test_cases.description: Calling record_tool_result on AgentTraceSink serializes tool_response via json.dumps with default=str, truncates if needed, and appends a tool.result event line to the audit JSONL file.
preconditions: A temporary audit directory exists at .agent-fox/audit/
An AgentTraceSink instance is initialized with a valid run_id pointing to agent_{run_id}.jsonl in the audit directory
The audit JSONL file exists and is writable

expected.audit_jsonl: One new line appended to agent_run-abc123.jsonl containing a JSON object with event_type='tool.result', run_id='run-abc123', node_id='node-1', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-001', and tool_response equal to the JSON-serialized string of the input dict

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: sink = AgentTraceSink(audit_dir); sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-abc123', node_id='node-1', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-001', tool_response={'stdout': 'hello world', 'exit_code': 0}); lines = read_jsonl('agent_run-abc123.jsonl'); event = parse_json(lines[-1]); assert event['event_type'] == 'tool.result'; assert event['run_id'] == 'run-abc123'; assert event['node_id'] == 'node-1'; assert event['tool_name'] == 'bash'; assert event['tool_use_id'] == 'tuid-001'; assert event['tool_response'] == json_dumps({'stdout': 'hello world', 'exit_code': 0}, default=str)

test_cases.description: Every tool.result event written by AgentTraceSink contains all required schema fields: event_type, run_id, timestamp (ISO 8601), node_id, tool_name, tool_use_id, and tool_response as a string.
preconditions: A temporary audit directory exists at .agent-fox/audit/
An AgentTraceSink instance is initialized with a valid run_id

expected.event_fields: Parsed JSON line has keys: event_type='tool.result', run_id (str), timestamp (ISO 8601 parseable string), node_id (str), tool_name (str), tool_use_id (str), tool_response (str)

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-schema-test', node_id='node-2', tool_name='read_file', tool_use_id='tuid-002', tool_response='file contents here'); event = parse_last_jsonl_line('agent_run-schema-test.jsonl'); assert event['event_type'] == 'tool.result'; assert isinstance(event['timestamp'], str); assert datetime.fromisoformat(event['timestamp']) is not None; assert event['tool_name'] == 'read_file'; assert event['tool_use_id'] == 'tuid-002'; assert isinstance(event['tool_response'], str)

test_cases.description: When tool_response serializes to more than 50000 characters, AgentTraceSink truncates the stored value to exactly 50000 chars and appends ' [truncated]'.
preconditions: A temporary audit directory exists at .agent-fox/audit/
An AgentTraceSink instance is initialized with a valid run_id

input.tool_response: A string that when JSON-serialized exceeds 50000 characters (e.g. 'x' * 60000)

expected.tool_response_length: The tool_response field in the written event is exactly 50000 + len(' [truncated]') = 50011 characters

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: long_response = 'x' * 60000; sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-trunc', node_id='node-3', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-003', tool_response=long_response); event = parse_last_jsonl_line('agent_run-trunc.jsonl'); stored = event['tool_response']; assert stored.endswith(' [truncated]'); assert len(stored) == 50000 + len(' [truncated]')

test_cases.description: Calling record_tool_result on SinkDispatcher forwards the call via _dispatch_optional to every registered sink that implements the method.
preconditions: A SinkDispatcher instance is created
A mock sink implementing record_tool_result is registered in the dispatcher
A second mock sink NOT implementing record_tool_result is also registered

expected.implementing_sink: record_tool_result is called once on the sink that implements it with the exact kwargs
expected.non_implementing_sink: No AttributeError or call is made on the sink that does not implement record_tool_result

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: implementing_sink = MockSink(has_record_tool_result=True); non_implementing_sink = MockSink(has_record_tool_result=False); dispatcher = SinkDispatcher([implementing_sink, non_implementing_sink]); dispatcher.record_tool_result(run_id='run-dispatch', node_id='node-4', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-004', tool_response='output'); assert implementing_sink.record_tool_result_calls == [{'run_id': 'run-dispatch', 'node_id': 'node-4', 'tool_name': 'bash', 'tool_use_id': 'tuid-004', 'tool_response': 'output'}]; assert non_implementing_sink.record_tool_result_calls == []

test_cases.description: Calling record_tool_result on a SinkDispatcher with no sinks implementing the method completes without raising any exception.
preconditions: A SinkDispatcher instance is created with one or more sinks that do NOT implement record_tool_result

expected.result: No exception is raised; the method returns None

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: non_implementing_sink = MockSink(has_record_tool_result=False); dispatcher = SinkDispatcher([non_implementing_sink]); result = dispatcher.record_tool_result(run_id='run-no-sink', node_id='node-5', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-005', tool_response='output'); assert result is None

test_cases.description: When ClaudeBackend.execute() is called with a non-None tool_result_callback, a PostToolUse hook is registered via HookMatcher following the same pattern as PostToolUseFailure.
preconditions: A ClaudeBackend instance is available
A mock tool_result_callback callable is prepared
The hooks dict is inspectable before SDK execution begins

expected.hooks_dict: hooks['PostToolUse'] is set to a list containing one HookMatcher instance wrapping the built hook function

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: callback = lambda **kw: None; captured_hooks = {}; with patch_hooks_capture(captured_hooks): backend.execute(..., tool_result_callback=callback); assert 'PostToolUse' in captured_hooks; assert len(captured_hooks['PostToolUse']) == 1; assert isinstance(captured_hooks['PostToolUse'][0], HookMatcher)

test_cases.description: When the PostToolUse SDK hook fires, the hook handler invokes tool_result_callback with tool_name, tool_use_id, and tool_response extracted from PostToolUseHookInput.
preconditions: A ClaudeBackend PostToolUse hook handler is built via _build_tool_result_hook(callback)
A mock PostToolUseHookInput is prepared with known tool_name, tool_use_id, and tool_response values

expected.callback_called_with: tool_result_callback is called once with tool_name='read_file', tool_use_id='tuid-007', tool_response='file content'

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: received = []; callback = lambda tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_response: received.append({'tool_name': tool_name, 'tool_use_id': tool_use_id, 'tool_response': tool_response}); hook = _build_tool_result_hook(callback); hook_input = MockPostToolUseHookInput(tool_name='read_file', tool_use_id='tuid-007', tool_response='file content'); hook(hook_input); assert len(received) == 1; assert received[0] == {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_use_id': 'tuid-007', 'tool_response': 'file content'}

test_cases.description: When ClaudeBackend.execute() is called with tool_result_callback=None, no PostToolUse hook is registered in the hooks dict.
preconditions: A ClaudeBackend instance is available
The hooks dict is inspectable before SDK execution begins

expected.hooks_dict: hooks does not contain the key 'PostToolUse'

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: captured_hooks = {}; with patch_hooks_capture(captured_hooks): backend.execute(..., tool_result_callback=None); assert 'PostToolUse' not in captured_hooks

test_cases.description: When _execute_query() is called with an active SinkDispatcher containing AgentTraceSink, it constructs a tool_result_callback that calls sink_dispatcher.record_tool_result with run_id, node_id, tool_name, tool_use_id, and tool_response, and passes it to ClaudeBackend.execute().

run_id and node_id are set in the _execute_query closure scope
ClaudeBackend.execute() is mocked to capture the tool_result_callback argument

expected.callback_behavior: Invoking the callback with tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-wire', tool_response='out' results in sink_dispatcher.record_tool_result being called with those exact kwargs plus run_id and node_id

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: mock_backend = MockClaudeBackend(); dispatcher = SinkDispatcher([AgentTraceSink(...)]); _execute_query(backend=mock_backend, sink_dispatcher=dispatcher, run_id='run-wire', node_id='node-wire', ...); captured_cb = mock_backend.last_execute_kwargs['tool_result_callback']; assert captured_cb is not None; with patch(dispatcher, 'record_tool_result') as mock_rtr: captured_cb(tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-wire', tool_response='out'); assert mock_rtr.called_with(run_id='run-wire', node_id='node-wire', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-wire', tool_response='out')

preconditions: A SinkDispatcher with NO AgentTraceSink registered is available
ClaudeBackend.execute() is mocked to capture the tool_result_callback argument
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: mock_backend = MockClaudeBackend(); dispatcher = SinkDispatcher([]); _execute_query(backend=mock_backend, sink_dispatcher=dispatcher, ...); assert mock_backend.last_execute_kwargs['tool_result_callback'] is None

test_cases.description: When --audit is active and a tool executes successfully, the audit JSONL file contains a tool.result event after the corresponding tool.use event with matching tool_name and tool_use_id.
preconditions: A temporary audit directory exists at .agent-fox/audit/
AgentTraceSink is initialized and registered in SinkDispatcher
A prior tool.use event with tool_use_id='tuid-e2e' has been written to the audit JSONL file

expected.audit_file: agent_run-e2e.jsonl contains a tool.result event after the tool.use event, with tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-e2e', and non-empty tool_response

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-e2e', node_id='node-e2e', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-e2e', tool_response='command output'); events = [parse_json(line) for line in read_lines('agent_run-e2e.jsonl')]; tool_use_idx = index_of(events, lambda e: e['event_type'] == 'tool.use' and e['tool_use_id'] == 'tuid-e2e'); tool_result_idx = index_of(events, lambda e: e['event_type'] == 'tool.result' and e['tool_use_id'] == 'tuid-e2e'); assert tool_result_idx > tool_use_idx; assert events[tool_result_idx]['tool_name'] == 'bash'; assert events[tool_result_idx]['tool_response'] != ''

test_cases.description: When a session completes with multiple tool calls under --audit, the audit JSONL file contains exactly one tool.result event per tool.use event, each with a matching tool_use_id.
preconditions: A temporary audit directory exists at .agent-fox/audit/
AgentTraceSink is initialized and registered in SinkDispatcher
Three tool.use events with distinct tool_use_ids have been written

expected.correlation: Each tool.result event's tool_use_id matches one of the tool.use events' tool_use_ids
expected.tool_result_count: Exactly 3 tool.result events in the audit JSONL file

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: for call in tool_calls: sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-multi', node_id='node-m', **call); events = [parse_json(line) for line in read_lines('agent_run-multi.jsonl')]; result_events = [e for e in events if e['event_type'] == 'tool.result']; assert len(result_events) == 3; result_ids = {e['tool_use_id'] for e in result_events}; assert result_ids == {'tuid-m1', 'tuid-m2', 'tuid-m3'}

test_cases.description: When --audit is NOT active, no tool.result events are written to any file during a session.
preconditions: A SinkDispatcher with NO AgentTraceSink registered is available
ClaudeBackend is configured with tool_result_callback=None
No audit JSONL file exists for the run

expected.audit_file: No file at .agent-fox/audit/agent_{run_id}.jsonl is created or modified; no line with event_type='tool.result' exists in any file

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: dispatcher = SinkDispatcher([]); backend = ClaudeBackend(); backend.execute(..., tool_result_callback=None); assert not file_exists('.agent-fox/audit/agent_run-noaudit.jsonl') OR (all lines in file do not have event_type == 'tool.result')

property_tests.description: For any tool invocation during an --audit session, the tool.result event with a given tool_use_id always appears after the tool.use event with the same tool_use_id in the audit JSONL file.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random tool_use_id strings (UUID4) and arbitrary tool_response values (strings, dicts, lists); write a tool.use event then call record_tool_result; parse all lines of the JSONL file
property_tests.invariant_check: for each tool_use_id: index_of(tool.result event) > index_of(tool.use event) in the ordered list of parsed JSONL lines

property_tests.description: For any pair of tool.use and tool.result events in the audit JSONL file, the tool_use_id field in the tool.result event equals the tool_use_id field in the corresponding tool.use event.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate sequences of 1-10 tool invocations, each with a unique UUID4 tool_use_id; write tool.use events then call record_tool_result for each; parse the JSONL file
property_tests.invariant_check: for each tool_use_id in the set of written IDs: exactly one tool.result event exists with that tool_use_id, and its tool_use_id == the tool_use_id of the corresponding tool.use event

property_tests.description: For any tool.result event written to the audit JSONL file, the length of the tool_response string never exceeds 50000 + len(' [truncated]') characters.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate tool_response values of varying sizes: strings of length 0, 1, 49999, 50000, 50001, 100000, and random lengths between 0 and 100000; also generate dicts and lists of varying sizes
property_tests.invariant_check: for each generated tool_response: after calling record_tool_result and parsing the written event, assert len(event['tool_response']) <= 50000 + len(' [truncated]')

property_tests.description: For any session run without --audit, no file in the filesystem contains a line with event_type equal to 'tool.result' attributable to that run.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random run_ids and simulate 1-5 tool executions per run with tool_result_callback=None; scan all files in .agent-fox/audit/ after each simulated run
property_tests.invariant_check: for each simulated run: no file in .agent-fox/audit/ contains a JSON line with event_type == 'tool.result' and run_id matching the simulated run_id

property_tests.description: For any exception raised inside the PostToolUse hook handler, the session continues to completion and subsequent tool calls are executed; the exception is logged as WARNING and not re-raised.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random exception types (RuntimeError, IOError, ValueError, TypeError) with random messages; build a hook handler with a callback that raises the generated exception; invoke the hook handler
property_tests.invariant_check: for each generated exception: hook(hook_input) returns without raising; at least one WARNING log entry is emitted; a subsequent call to hook(hook_input2) also completes without raising

property_tests.description: For any session with N successful tool invocations under --audit, the audit JSONL file contains exactly N tool.result events.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate N in range 0-20; simulate N successful tool invocations by calling record_tool_result N times with distinct tool_use_ids; parse the JSONL file
property_tests.invariant_check: count of lines with event_type == 'tool.result' in the JSONL file == N

property_tests.description: For any value of tool_response passed to AgentTraceSink.record_tool_result, json.dumps(tool_response, default=str) completes without raising a TypeError regardless of the runtime type.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate diverse tool_response values: None, bool, int, float, str, list, dict, set, bytes, custom class instances, datetime objects, nested structures with mixed types
property_tests.invariant_check: for each generated value: json.dumps(value, default=str) does not raise TypeError; the result is a non-empty string

edge_case_tests.description: When tool_response is None or an unserializable custom type, AgentTraceSink.record_tool_result uses json.dumps default=str to coerce the value and still writes the event without raising.
preconditions: A temporary audit directory exists at .agent-fox/audit/
An AgentTraceSink instance is initialized with a valid run_id

expected.event_written: A tool.result event is appended to agent_run-none-resp.jsonl with tool_response equal to the string 'null' (JSON serialization of None)
expected.no_exception: No TypeError or other exception is raised

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: sink = AgentTraceSink(audit_dir); sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-none-resp', node_id='node-e1', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-e1', tool_response=None); event = parse_last_jsonl_line('agent_run-none-resp.jsonl'); assert event['event_type'] == 'tool.result'; assert event['tool_response'] == 'null'; also test with CustomUnserializableObject: sink.record_tool_result(..., tool_response=CustomObj()); event2 = parse_last_jsonl_line(...); assert isinstance(event2['tool_response'], str)

edge_case_tests.description: When tool_response is an empty string, empty dict, or empty list, AgentTraceSink serializes it normally and writes the event without special-casing.
preconditions: A temporary audit directory exists at .agent-fox/audit/
An AgentTraceSink instance is initialized with a valid run_id

expected.event_written: For each case, a tool.result event is written with tool_response equal to the JSON-serialized empty value

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: for (response, expected_str) in [('', '""'), ({}, '{}'), ([], '[]')]: sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-empty', node_id='node-e2', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-e2', tool_response=response); event = parse_last_jsonl_line('agent_run-empty.jsonl'); assert event['tool_response'] == expected_str

edge_case_tests.description: When _write_event raises an IOError (e.g. disk full), AgentTraceSink.record_tool_result propagates the IOError to the caller without swallowing it.
preconditions: An AgentTraceSink instance is initialized
_write_event is patched to raise IOError('disk full')
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: sink = AgentTraceSink(audit_dir); with patch(sink, '_write_event', raises=IOError('disk full')): try: sink.record_tool_result(run_id='run-ioerr', node_id='node-e3', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-e3', tool_response='output'); assert False, 'Expected IOError'; except IOError as e: assert str(e) == 'disk full'

edge_case_tests.description: When one registered sink's record_tool_result raises an exception during SinkDispatcher dispatch, the behavior is consistent with existing _dispatch_optional error semantics (log and continue or propagate).
preconditions: A SinkDispatcher instance is created
A mock sink whose record_tool_result raises RuntimeError('sink failure') is registered
A second mock sink that implements record_tool_result successfully is also registered

expected.behavior: The behavior matches the existing _dispatch_optional error semantics; the second sink's record_tool_result is called (if _dispatch_optional continues on error) or the exception propagates (if _dispatch_optional re-raises)

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: failing_sink = MockSink(record_tool_result=raises(RuntimeError('sink failure'))); good_sink = MockSink(record_tool_result=records_call); dispatcher = SinkDispatcher([failing_sink, good_sink]); try: dispatcher.record_tool_result(run_id='run-sink-err', node_id='node-e4', tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-e4', tool_response='output'); except Exception: pass; # verify behavior matches _dispatch_optional contract for other optional methods

edge_case_tests.description: When tool_result_callback raises an exception inside the PostToolUse hook handler, the handler catches it, logs a WARNING, and does not re-raise, allowing session execution to continue.
preconditions: A ClaudeBackend PostToolUse hook handler is built via _build_tool_result_hook(callback)
The callback is configured to raise RuntimeError('callback failed')
A logging capture fixture is active

expected.no_exception: No exception propagates out of the hook handler
expected.return_value: The hook handler returns normally (returns None)
expected.warning_logged: A WARNING-level log entry is emitted containing the error details ('callback failed')

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: callback = lambda **kw: raise RuntimeError('callback failed'); hook = _build_tool_result_hook(callback); hook_input = MockPostToolUseHookInput(tool_name='bash', tool_use_id='tuid-e5', tool_response='output'); with capture_logs() as logs: result = hook(hook_input); assert result is None; warning_logs = [l for l in logs if l.level == 'WARNING']; assert len(warning_logs) >= 1; assert 'callback failed' in warning_logs[0].message

edge_case_tests.description: When PostToolUseHookInput has missing or unexpected fields, the hook handler catches AttributeError or KeyError, logs a WARNING, and does not call tool_result_callback.
preconditions: A ClaudeBackend PostToolUse hook handler is built via _build_tool_result_hook(callback)
A malformed hook input object is prepared that raises AttributeError when tool_name is accessed
A logging capture fixture is active

expected.no_exception: No exception propagates out of the hook handler
expected.warning_logged: A WARNING-level log entry is emitted

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: call_count = [0]; callback = lambda **kw: call_count.__setitem__(0, call_count[0]+1); hook = _build_tool_result_hook(callback); malformed_input = MalformedHookInput(); with capture_logs() as logs: result = hook(malformed_input); assert result is None; assert call_count[0] == 0; warning_logs = [l for l in logs if l.level == 'WARNING']; assert len(warning_logs) >= 1

edge_case_tests.description: Other backends (deepagents, google_adk) do not accept or register a tool_result_callback; the parameter is exclusive to ClaudeBackend.execute().

expected.deepagents: DeepAgentsBackend.execute() does not have a tool_result_callback parameter

smoke_tests.description: Happy path end-to-end: a tool executes during an --audit session and a tool.result event is appended to the audit JSONL file with correct fields.
smoke_tests.trigger: Operator launches nightshift with --audit; a tool is invoked by the model; the PostToolUse hook fires and the full chain from ClaudeBackend through SinkDispatcher to AgentTraceSink writes the event.
mockable: claude_agent_sdk (PostToolUse hook firing — inject a synthetic PostToolUseHookInput)
expected_effects: agent_{run_id}.jsonl exists in the temporary audit directory
The last line of agent_{run_id}.jsonl is valid JSON with event_type='tool.result'
The event contains tool_name, tool_use_id, node_id, run_id, timestamp, and tool_response fields
tool_response is a non-empty string (JSON-serialized tool output)
No exception is raised during the entire chain

smoke_tests.description: Hook failure path: when the tool_result_callback raises an exception inside the PostToolUse hook, the handler catches it, logs a WARNING, and session execution continues.
smoke_tests.trigger: The PostToolUse hook fires; the tool_result_callback raises an IOError; the ClaudeBackend hook handler catches it and returns normally.
expected_effects: The hook handler returns None without re-raising the IOError
